user.description: Detected: {detected}. Backups run nightly and are stored under /config/{backup_dir}/, so they are included in Home Assistant's own backups. Schedule, retention and the watchdog heartbeat can be changed later under Configure.

data_description.backup_time: Local time. Default 03:17 avoids the 03:00 Home Assistant backup rush.
data_description.max_restore_age_days: A restore from a very old backup leaves recently added devices orphaned. Only the radio_guard.restore action's force option can override this.
data_description.offline_minutes: Counted only after Home Assistant has fully started, so restarts and slow boots never trigger it.

data.z2m_data_dir: Data folder (only if Zigbee2MQTT is not the add-on)

data_description.z2m_base_topic: Must match base_topic in Zigbee2MQTT's MQTT settings.
data_description.z2m_data_dir: Where Home Assistant sees Zigbee2MQTT's data folder, for example /config/zigbee2mqtt or /share/zigbee2mqtt. Needed to restore a Zigbee2MQTT that runs in its own container.

heartbeat.name: Watchdog heartbeat (MQTT)
heartbeat.description: Publishes a liveness message an external power watchdog can monitor. Requires the MQTT integration.

wiz_pick.title: Move your {source} network to a new coordinator
wiz_pick.description:
Radio Guard copies your network from a backup onto a new coordinator, so you don't have to re-pair any devices. You only swap the hardware when asked.

Choose the backup to restore. The newest is usually right; pick an older one only if the coordinator was misbehaving before it failed.

wiz_migrate.title: Move to a new {source} coordinator
wiz_migrate.description:
Radio Guard moves your network from the coordinator you use now onto a new one, without re-pairing any devices.

**Now in use:** {ieee} on `{port}`, {devices} devices

1. Radio Guard takes a fresh backup of this coordinator.
2. {source} stops and you swap the hardware.
3. Your network is written to the new coordinator, {source} starts again and your devices are asked to report in.

The old coordinator is not changed, so you can go back to it at the end.

wiz_swap.title: Swap the coordinator

data.companion_port: Second radio on the same stick

data_description.port: Leave as is if the new coordinator uses the same port as the old one.
data_description.network_address: For example 192.168.1.50 or tcp://slzb-06.local:6638. Port 6638 is assumed if you leave it out.
data_description.companion_port: The matching port of your new stick. Leave as is.

abort.recovery_sheet:
[Open your recovery sheet]({url})

It lists your hardware, where your backups are and what to do when a radio or this machine fails. Print it, or save it as a PDF somewhere you can reach when Home Assistant is down, and keep it with your spare hardware.

backup_now.name: Back up now
backup_now.description: Pull a fresh coordinator backup. Omit source to back up all enabled coordinators.

list_backups.name: List backups
list_backups.description: Return the stored backups per coordinator, newest first.

restore.name: Restore
restore.description: Overwrites the attached coordinator with a stored network backup. Dry run by default: reports what would happen and raises a notification without changing anything.

file.name: Backup file
file.description: File name from list_backups. Defaults to the newest.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Dry run only checks; restore performs it.

force.name: Force
force.description: Proceed even if the pre-flight reports a blocking problem. For Silicon Labs radios this also permits a one-time IEEE overwrite.

source_not_enabled.message: {source} is not enabled in Radio Guard. Add it under Configure.

restore_blocked.message: {source} restore blocked by pre-flight: {reasons} Run a dry run for details, or set force to override.
